auxiliary_lookups.purpose: Read-only documentation check after two auto-mode classifier denials of the committer's git add ('Credential Leakage'): how permission allow rules interact with the auto-mode classifier, whether subagents inherit them, how an owner can pre-authorize specific commands or approve a denied action, and what the owner-side options are. No settings are changed.

documented: Deny and ask permission rules are evaluated before the classifier; an ask rule forces a prompt even in auto mode.

The classifier reads 'autoMode' configuration only from user settings (~/.claude/settings.json), managed settings or --settings/SDK; not from project .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json.
Subagents inherit the main session's auto mode; a frontmatter permissionMode is ignored when the main session is in auto mode.
The classifier reads the user's messages and the commands run, not their output.
A user message that names the action and its specific danger can clear a soft-deny block for that one action; naming the verb alone does not.
The /permissions 'Recently denied' retry is a one-off terminal UI approval (terminal dialogs are not available in this desktop session).
inferred_or_unknown: The 'Credential Leakage' rule wording is not published.
Whether a subagent's classifier sees the main conversation's user messages is not stated explicitly; the earlier 'Instruction Poisoning' case cleared after the owner's direct message.
The lookup's statements on how allow rules interact with the classifier are partly inconsistent; treat them as unverified.
coordinator_constraints: Agents change no permission or global settings (AGENTS rule 3); any settings change is the owner's own action.
No retry without a changed condition (a new owner message naming the action and its danger, a manual commit, or an owner-made settings change).
